clue.text: Tetanus jabs are welcomed at first by key partner

parts.note: a lock is what a key is paired with

indicators.note: tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A patient with tetanus is given injections, welcomed early on by a partner holding the key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key partner' looks like a person, but it is the thing a key goes with.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the everyday name for tetanus, after the clenched jaw it causes.

clue.text: Find, see and hear one asked for a kiss

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: signals that the name is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Kate, from the musical Kiss Me, Kate

explanation.surface: Track down someone who has been asked for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter's musical 'Kiss Me, Kate' makes Kate the one asked for a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find where it is, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Grounds where copper leaves political meetings

indicators.note: copper goes away from the word, so its letters are dropped

parts.note: caucuses are meetings of party members
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman walks out of party meetings on good grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; here it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are reasons or motives, which is what causes means here.

clue.text: Not a lot of uniform stock in green

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: jade is a shade of green
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a stash is a hidden store

explanation.surface: A small amount of uniform supplies held in green.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means only slightly, a small amount, which is not a lot.

clue.text: Drew a tangled knot, perhaps

indicators.note: a tangle is a twisted mess, so the letters of drew and a are twisted around

explanation.surface: Someone sketched a twisted knot of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' looks like a tie in rope, but it is a shore bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a sandpiper, so it is an example of a long-legged shore bird.

clue.text: Previously enters poor clue for "anorak"

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other, splitting it
something poor is in bad shape, so the word clue is to be knocked into a new order

parts.note: previously means ago, as in 'years ago'

explanation.surface: A crossword editor notes that a weak clue for the word anorak was entered earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' is in quotes because it is the garment, not the British slang for an obsessive nerd.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a light hooded waterproof jacket, the same garment as an anorak.

clue.text: Album includes screen shot — love the build-up!

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is an album

indicators.note: a shot item is ruined, so the letters of screen are messed up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: An album features a shot from the screen and the fan enjoys the rising tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as a photograph in the surface, but in the parse it means ruined, so it reorders the letters of screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness or intensity, a build-up.

clue.text: Playing tricks, try to hug a compiler and start to blush — cool!

indicators.note: one piece wraps around another as in an embrace

parts.note: a go is an attempt
the setter of the puzzle refers to themself as me

indicators.note: the first letter of blush is set inside the word for cool, joined on by and

parts.note: a fridge keeps things cool

indicators.note: only the opening letter of blush is used

explanation.surface: A prankster tries to embrace the crossword setter, who blushes: very cool.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not strictly say the blush letter goes inside the word for cool; 'and' has to stand for that. 'Playing tricks' is the card sense: tricks are won in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game played by winning tricks, so a game of bridge involves playing tricks.

clue.text: Visiting Luxor, I ousted loving wife

indicators.note: the answer pays a visit inside these words, sitting among their letters

explanation.surface: On a trip to Luxor, a man threw out his adoring spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorious describes a man excessively fond of his wife, so doting on one's spouse.

clue.text: They plan to generate total heat

indicators.note: generating produces something new, so the letters of they plan are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Engineers' scheme to produce overall heat.
explanation.definitionFit: In thermodynamics enthalpy is the total heat content of a system.

clue.text: Alternative to part of 18 in bid for 6 beats

definitions.text: Alternative to part of 18 in bid for 6
definitions.meaning: 18 is a bid of five diamonds in the game of 6, bridge; another suit could replace diamonds
to beat someone with a cudgel is to strike them with a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A bridge player weighs another suit in place of diamonds, and thrashes the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point to FIVE DIAMONDS (18) and GAME OF BRIDGE (6); swapping the suit gives the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four card suits, and as a verb it means strikes with a heavy stick.

clue.text: Paper snake in empty dessert dish

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports a snake found lying in a bowl that once held pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like crockery after 'dessert', but it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for a very attractive person, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Artists as a body follow a competitive lifestyle

parts.note: the RA, the Royal Academy of Arts, is the body of British artists
to trace someone is to follow their trail

explanation.surface: Artists collectively are said to pursue a cut-throat career.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the idiom for an exhausting, competitive struggle to get ahead at work.

clue.text: Republicans in Iraq briefly feature in admirable air composed by Gershwin

indicators.note: the letters feature, sitting unbroken, inside the word admirable

explanation.surface: A rambling tale of republicans in Iraq and a lovely tune by Gershwin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers four routes to the same letters: IRAQ cut short ('briefly'), letters hidden in 'admirable' ('feature in'), the reworking of AIR, and Ira Gershwin, the lyricist brother of George.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Republican Army is the paramilitary group usually called simply the republicans.

clue.text: Feature of food that could lead to digestion stress with spare tires

indicators.note: the combined letters could be rearranged to produce something else
spare means set aside, so the letters of tires are left out of the pool

explanation.surface: Heavy food can cause digestive trouble and a spare tyre round the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix DIGESTION and STRESS, take out the letters of TIRES, and the rest rearrange; 'spare tires' is also US belly fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodginess is heaviness and stodge, the filling dense quality of a dish.

clue.text: The tenor's wobbly bottom in bid for 6

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady, so the letters of the tenor are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of 'the tenor', the possessive 's adding none
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: An opera singer's rear end shakes alarmingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is GAME OF BRIDGE; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Three no-trump is a contract called in bridge, undertaking nine tricks with no trump suit.

clue.text: Blurt that European currency unit's dead without Angela Merkel's approval

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the currency unit goes round the German yes

parts.note: the ECU was the European Currency Unit; the 's is a link
ja is German for yes
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the euro's forerunner died without the German chancellor's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejaculate in its older sense means to exclaim suddenly, to blurt out.

clue.text: See 6
Service, say, includes 6 but excludes 1

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'say' wraps around the rest

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

indicators.note: the numeral one, as the letter I, is removed from the word

parts.note: 6 is the answer GAME; read in its other sense, game is wild meat such as venison
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A church service, for instance, takes in item six but leaves out item one.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 looks like a cross-reference to the bridge answer, but GAME is taken in its meat sense; 'excludes 1' removes I from VENISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.

clue.text: Bid for 6 could lead to vice

parts.note: in bridge shorthand the bid is written V D, Roman five and D for the suit; VD, venereal disease, is what vice could lead to

explanation.surface: A warning that a bid at the card table can be a slippery slope to sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Five is V in Roman numerals and the suit is written D, so the bid looks like VD, a disease vice could lead to.
explanation.definitionFit: Five diamonds is a bridge contract to take eleven tricks with diamonds as trumps.

clue.text: Diggers' alternative to 20 in bid for 6

definitions.meaning: 20 is hearts, part of the bridge bid four hearts; another suit could stand in

explanation.surface: Gardeners' tools offered in place of hearts at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are both garden tools for digging and one of the four card suits.

clue.text: See 24
Streak with no clothing, drunk

indicators.note: stripping the word drunk of its outer layer leaves only its inside letters

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy goes streaking naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streak' and 'no clothing' suggest a naked dash, but the definition means a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A run is an unbroken series, like a winning streak.

clue.text: Interrogate family on odd price for food

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them for information
kin are relatives

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of price are taken

explanation.surface: Questioning relatives about a strange price for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpkin pie is a dessert, a sweet tart filled with spiced squash, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Dad's half-hearted talk

indicators.note: one of the pair of letters at the heart of the word is lost

parts.note: patter is glib talk

explanation.surface: A father's chat lacks conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Spooner's unchaste lady cuts one bid for 6

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: a whore is a prostitute
to cut one is slang for breaking wind

explanation.surface: A lady of easy virtue lets one go at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'whore' and 'farts' gives the bid; 'cut one' is British slang for passing wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Four hearts is a bridge contract to take ten tricks with hearts as trumps.

clue.text: Occasional dab of refreshment applied primarily in pit

definitions.text: Occasional dab of refreshment applied primarily in pit

indicators.note: the initials go inside the word for a pit

parts.note: a dent is a small pit or hollow

indicators.note: taking the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A little freshening product dabbed now and then into the armpit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the product: 'pit' doubles as armpit.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints the use of an underarm freshener, dabbed into the armpit.

clue.text: Bush Senior

definitions.meaning: a shrub with white flowers and dark berries
older, as in an older person of standing

explanation.surface: George H W Bush, the father, as opposed to his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder is both a shrub of the honeysuckle family and a word for older or senior.

clue.text: Take a defensive position when grenade explodes

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the pieces, so the letters of grenade are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told to take cover when a grenade goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencing call tells a fencer to adopt the guard stance, ready to defend.

clue.text: Revolution for some feminists is erudite and does not surrender

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run across its words

explanation.surface: A learned woman sees feminism as revolution and will not give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight back and refuse to yield, the opposite of giving in.
